Z <- alpha * as.matrix(A %*% X)     if (is.null(Y) || beta == 0) Z else Z + beta * Y   },   apply_adjoint = function(X, alpha = 1, beta = 0, Y = NULL) {     Z <- alpha * as.matrix(crossprod(A, X))     if (is.null(Y) || beta == 0) Z else Z + beta * Y   },   name = "matrix-free A" ) fit_mf <- svd_partial(op, rank = 5, target = largest()) fit_mf$certificate$norm_bound_type #> [1] "frobenius_hutchinson_estimate" op_hinted <- linear_operator(   dim = dim(A),   apply = op$apply,   apply_adjoint = op$apply_adjoint,   name = "matrix-free A (exact norm)",   metadata = list(frobenius_norm = norm(A, type = "F")) ) fit_hinted <- svd_partial(op_hinted, rank = 5, target = largest()) fit_hinted$certificate$norm_bound_type #> [1] "frobenius_metadata" fit_hinted$certificate$passed #> [1] TRUE

what: How do you reuse the previous eigenspace?
title: Reuse an eigenspace across a parameter sweep
text: Pass returned eigenvectors next solve. values alone enough: initial_subspace expects directions one row per operator dimension. pattern extends sweep. example also runs cold solve step work answers can compared equal terms. reproducible family, every continuation step uses fewer operator columns cold counterpart agrees requested values well within solve tolerance. counts include work used guard certify supplied subspace; operator_block_calls different metric one block call may apply operator several columns. assume speedup every sweep. target eigenspace changes abruptly supplied directions little overlap , warm solve can cost much cold one. reproducible benchmark inst/benchmarks/bench-warm-start-continuation.R includes high-overlap continuation deliberate overlap-loss jump.
code: rho <- 0.02 warm <- eig_partial(   A - rho * B, k = k, target = smallest(), method = method,   tol = 1e-8, seed = 2026, initial_subspace = vectors(first) ) certificate(warm)$passed #> [1] TRUE rhos <- c(0.02, 0.04, 0.06) start <- vectors(first) rows <- vector("list", length(rhos))  for (i in seq_along(rhos)) {   op <- A - rhos[[i]] * B   cold <- eig_partial(     op, k, smallest(), method = method, tol = 1e-8, seed = 2026   )   warm <- eig_partial(     op, k, smallest(), method = method, tol = 1e-8, seed = 2026,     initial_subspace = start   )   rows[[i]] <- data.frame(     rho = rhos[[i]],     cold_columns = cold$operator_columns,     warm_columns = warm$operator_columns,     max_value_difference = max(abs(sort(values(cold)) - sort(values(warm))))   )   start <- vectors(warm) } comparison <- do.call(rbind, rows)

Rank detection invariant column scaling, fitted start block orthonormal. start treated hint — every solve recomputes projected quantities, residuals, orthogonality, convergence, fresh current-operator certificate. fully supplied subspace already invariant requested tolerance discarded cold start: residual certification proves eigenpair accuracy, invariant block contains requested extremal pairs. initial_subspace = NULL preserves cold behavior exactly. Unsupported generalized, shift-invert, dense-fallback plans error. Results, plans, diagnostics() report start provenance plus exact operator block calls, operator columns, certification columns. Reusable restart-state objects generalized/transformed promotion remain future work. lanczos() gains check_stride. default 0L preserves full-sweep convergence checks exactly; positive stride lets native block thick-restart paths, including real Hermitian matrix-free callbacks, check stop within sweep without additional operator applications.

title: eigencore 1.1.0 (2026-08-24)
text: Sparse tridiagonal shift-invert now parses validates three matrix bands per solve reuses immutable representation planning, shift perturbation, factorization, certification. native kernel forms returns requested Ritz vectors instead exposing full Krylov basis R. installed path_laplacian:1000, k = 20 release row reduced cumulative R allocation 3.82 MB 1.51 MB retaining 20/20 original-coordinate certificate. G1 gate now uses retained result size bounded memory envelope reports bench::mem_alloc separately diagnostic evidence, R allocation counters observe native C/C++ working heaps compared engine. New production auto route largest-target partial SVD: native implicit normal-equations (Gram) thick-restart Lanczos runs   operator, without materializing Gram matrix. covers dense matrices sparse operators whose smaller side exceeds explicit-Gram caps — regimes previously fell back full LAPACK SVD (dense) single unrestarted Golub-Kahan sweep (sparse). Representative -machine speedups tol = 1e-8 certificates still passing: dense 4000x1000 k = 10 ~12x, dense 2000x2000 k = 10 ~80x, sparse 20000x5000 k = 10 k = 50 ~2x. Results keep exact two-sided residual certificate original coordinates, uncertified results still fall back native Golub-Kahan path. scalar Golub-Kahan kernel now uses BLAS (dgemv) classical Gram-Schmidt reorthogonalization sparse CSC, matrix-free, retained-restart paths, matching dense path; previously used scalar loops. projected Golub-Kahan convergence check now runs dbdsqr directly projected bidiagonal, tracking last row left singular vectors, instead dense dgesvd full vectors; scratch buffers reused across checks. check drops O(iter^3) plus per-check allocations O(iter^2). scalar Lanczos convergence estimate (used shift-invert paths) computes eigenvalues dsterf recovers selected eigenvectors dstevr instead full dstev decomposition iteration, scratch reuse across iterations. CSC sparse matrix-multiply kernel now processes wide blocks cache-friendly chunks 10 columns instead strided generic loop. as_operator() longer forces full copy already-double dense matrix (storage.mode<- now conditional), removing O(m*n) copy plus GC churn every problem construction — operator construction 2000x2000 input drops ~52ms ~6ms. scalar thick-restart Hermitian Lanczos default subspace grows 3k+20 max(3k+20, 5k): unchanged small k, k = 30 general sparse operator cuts operator applications ~25%.

title: eigencore 1.0.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-07-23 First CRAN release. svd_partial() eig_partial() compute top-k singular triplets eigenpairs large dense, sparse (CSC), diagonal, banded/tridiagonal, matrix-free operators native C++ kernels. Every result carries numerical certificate: residuals singular relations, backward-error bound, orthogonality loss, labeled norm bound, single passed flag. Bounds can estimated (example stochastic norm estimates centered sparse operators) reported estimates never produce unqualified passed. Operator algebra — center(), scale_cols(), compose(), crossprod_operator(), linear_operator() — solves centered, scaled, composed problems without forming dense matrices. Transparent method selection: plan_solver() reports chosen kernel solve, fit$method names path actually ran. Problem classes without production kernel carry explicit reference labels. RSpectra-compatible wrappers eigs(), eigs_sym(), svds() accept codes additionally return certificates. Benchmarked ‘RSpectra’, ‘irlba’, ‘PRIMME’; reproduce Rscript inst/benchmarks/bench-readme.R. Generalized eigen support: eig_full() dense SPD general pencils, generalized_schur() generalized_svd() dense QZ/GSVD, partial sparse general pencils nonsingular diagonal B via transformed native Arnoldi, left eigenvectors conditioning diagnostics supported dense paths, pencil_norm_scaled alpha/beta classification. Sparse SPD partial paths remain eig_partial() / LOBPCG / B-orthogonal Lanczos; general sparse QZ non-diagonal sparse B explicit unsupported boundaries. real dense GSVD path currently requires linked LAPACK provides deprecated dggsvd routine. exported API stable 1.0.0; breaking changes follow semantic versioning.
